posts.title: Benchmarking eleven differential transcript usage tools on long-read RNA-seq with spike-in ground truth
posts.authors: Okafor N, Lindqvist E, Marsh T, et al.
posts.summary: The authors sequenced a mixture of cell lines with synthetic spike-in isoforms on both nanopore and PacBio, then scored eleven DTU tools against the known truth. Tools built for short reads lost much of their power on long-read counts, while two methods that model read-to-isoform assignment uncertainty held up best.
key_points: Spike-in mixes at three known ratios give a ground truth for isoform switching.
False discovery rates were badly calibrated for most tools below 10 reads per isoform.
Results were consistent between nanopore direct cDNA and PacBio Kinnex libraries.

figure.caption: Fig. 1 | F1 score for detecting isoform switches in the spike-in mixes, by tool and platform.
figure.credit: Example figure drawn for this preview

posts.title: Subcellular spatial transcriptomics maps tumour–stroma boundaries in bone sarcomas
posts.authors: Ferreira L, Han J, Achebe C, et al.
posts.summary: Imaging-based spatial profiling of 41 resected bone tumours located a thin band of transitional cells at the tumour edge. These cells co-expressed matrix remodelling and hypoxia programs and were enriched in samples from patients who later relapsed.
key_points: A 480-gene panel plus custom probes for sarcoma driver fusions.
Boundary cells were defined computationally by distance to stromal neighbours.
The boundary signature was checked against two public bulk RNA-seq cohorts.

figure.caption: Fig. 1 | Cells in one resected tumour section coloured by region: tumour, boundary band and stroma.
figure.credit: Example figure drawn for this preview

posts.title: scVelo-free RNA velocity from metabolic labelling in a single sequencing run
posts.authors: Brandt K, Osei A, Liu W, et al.
posts.summary: A combinatorial-indexing protocol that labels newly made RNA with 4sU lets the authors estimate transcription and decay rates per cell without relying on spliced and unspliced read ratios. The estimates agreed with time-course experiments better than splicing-based velocity.
key_points: Works on fixed cells, so samples can be pooled across days.
T-to-C conversion calls are made with a new error model for low-coverage reads.
Velocity streams in haematopoiesis matched known lineage order.

figure.caption: Labelled (new) RNA carries T>C conversions; comparing new and total RNA gives a velocity arrow for each cell.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Exitron splicing creates recurrent neoantigens across 9,000 tumours
posts.authors: Moreau P, Iyer S, Takahashi R, et al.
posts.summary: Re-analysis of pan-cancer RNA-seq found exitron splicing events that recur in specific tumour types and shift the reading frame. Several predicted peptides were detected by immunopeptidomics in matched samples.
key_points: Exitron calls required support from split reads in at least 5% of samples per cancer type.
Frame-shifting exitrons were enriched in tumours with spliceosome mutations.
Peptide hits came from 38 samples with matched mass-spec data.

figure.caption: An exitron inside a coding exon is spliced out, shifting the reading frame and producing a new peptide shown on MHC.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: A foundation model of full-length mRNA predicts isoform half-life
posts.authors: Weiss D, Nakamura Y, Petrov I, et al.
posts.summary: The model is trained on mature transcript sequences from many species and learns embeddings that separate isoforms of the same gene. A linear probe on these embeddings predicted mRNA half-life better than models trained on the 3′ UTR alone.
key_points: Contrastive training pairs orthologous and paralogous transcripts.
Embeddings are released for every GENCODE transcript.
Gains were largest for genes with alternative last exons.

figure.caption: Full-length transcripts go through one encoder; the embeddings separate isoforms and predict mRNA half-life.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Cell-type deconvolution of bulk RNA-seq is biased by tumour purity in ways reference choice cannot fix
posts.authors: Grant H, Oyelaran F, Zhou M, et al.
posts.summary: Using pseudo-bulk mixtures built from single-cell atlases, the authors show that seven deconvolution methods over-estimate immune fractions in low-purity tumours. Swapping in tissue-matched references reduced but did not remove the bias.
key_points: Bias scaled with how much the malignant cells resembled their tissue of origin.
Bayesian methods that model a tumour-specific expression profile performed best.
The authors provide a correction based on estimated purity.

figure.caption: At low tumour purity, estimated immune fractions come out higher than the true fractions.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Ultra-low-input total RNA-seq from single organoid crypts
posts.authors: Svensson A, Kariuki J, Romero C, et al.
posts.summary: A ribosomal-RNA depletion step that works on picogram inputs lets the authors capture non-polyadenylated RNA from individual organoid crypts. Intronic and histone mRNA reads gave a readout of cell-cycle stage that poly-A libraries miss.
key_points: Depletion efficiency stayed above 95% down to 10 pg of input.
Library cost is estimated at under $4 per sample.
Protocol and plate layouts are on protocols.io.

posts.title: Allele-specific expression in 2,300 human brains links eQTLs to isoform choice
posts.authors: Abara U, Novak M, Chen Y, et al.
posts.summary: Phased long-read data from a subset of donors showed that many variants called as expression QTLs act by shifting which isoform is made, not how much of the gene is expressed.
key_points: Haplotype-resolved isoforms from 180 donors anchored the short-read analysis.
About a third of eQTL genes had a matching isoform-ratio QTL.
Several hits overlap risk loci for psychiatric traits.

figure.caption: Two haplotypes give the same total expression but favour different isoforms.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Fast pseudoalignment for direct RNA nanopore reads with modification calls
posts.authors: Laine R, Mbeki T, Ortiz S, et al.
posts.summary: A k-mer index tolerant of nanopore error profiles quantifies transcripts from direct RNA reads about forty times faster than alignment. m6A calls are carried through so modification rates are reported per isoform.
key_points: Runs on a laptop for a full flow cell.
Isoform quantification correlated at 0.94 with alignment-based counts.
Outputs a tidy table that reads straight into R.

posts.title: Batch effects in multi-site single-cell atlases are dominated by dissociation time
posts.authors: Petersen L, Adeyemi K, Rossi G, et al.
posts.summary: In a controlled design where the same tissues were processed at five sites, time from resection to dissociation explained more variance than site or chemistry. A stress-gene score predicted which samples integration methods would over-correct.
key_points: Dissociation time was logged to the minute for every sample.
Integration methods differed most in how they handled stressed cells.
The stress score is a 24-gene list released with the paper.

posts.title: Targeted long-read sequencing of fusion transcripts from FFPE tissue
posts.authors: Haddad S, Kim E, Duarte F, et al.
posts.summary: Hybrid capture of fusion partner genes followed by nanopore sequencing recovered full-length fusion transcripts from archival FFPE blocks up to 15 years old, including breakpoints missed by a clinical short-read panel.
key_points: Median read length from FFPE was about 900 bases after repair.
Detected 4 fusions missed by the clinical assay in 60 samples.
Full-length reads showed which fusion isoforms keep the kinase domain.
